questions.prompt: You delegate to Explore and it returns paths only. You wanted it to also fix the two files it found. What actually blocked it?
options: Its prompt says "never edit", and it over-applied the instruction
Write and Edit are not in its tool pool, so there was no way to comply
It stopped early because CLAUDE.md told it not to modify anything
Read-only agents report findings by design and a follow-up run is needed
questions.explanation: Denied here means absent from the tool pool, not discouraged in prose — the capability isn't there, so no amount of re-prompting makes it possible. Option A invents a prompt the built-ins don't carry. Option C gets the mechanism backwards: Explore doesn't load CLAUDE.md at all, so no rule there could have stopped it. Option D is a workaround, not an explanation of the block.

questions.prompt: Your CLAUDE.md says "never modify anything under vendor/". You delegate to Explore to map the vendor directory's contents and it walks straight through it. Why?
options: Explore overrides CLAUDE.md by design for discovery work
The rule was too deep in the file for Explore to find
Explore starts without CLAUDE.md, so the rule was never in its window
CLAUDE.md applies only to the main conversation and only for writes
questions.explanation: Explore and Plan deliberately start with no CLAUDE.md and no git status, so your rules are simply absent from their startup context — the fix is to restate the rule in the delegation message. Option A describes the same gap as if it were an override policy, which misleads you into thinking a setting exists. Option B is wrong because the whole file is skipped, not part of it. Option D is backwards: the rule governs the main conversation too.

questions.prompt: You want to explore a risky refactor, try two approaches in parallel from where you are now, and keep both attempts out of your main window. Which is the best fit?
options: Two forks of the current conversation
A skill with context: fork, invoked twice
questions.explanation: Forks inherit the entire parent conversation, which is exactly the requirement here — you want each attempt to start from everything already established instead of re-explaining it, and each fork's tool calls still stay out of your window. general-purpose and Explore both start fresh, so you'd pay to rebuild the context twice. Option D is the inverse: a forked skill gets the skill content as its prompt and still can't see your conversation.

questions.prompt: You need to find out what a stack trace in the conversation two turns ago actually meant. Which is the right tool?
options: Explore, asking it to read the terminal output
general-purpose, passing the trace text in the prompt
/btw, which sees your full context and has no tool access
A custom subagent with Read and Bash
questions.explanation: /btw exists for exactly this shape: the answer is about what's already in your conversation, so it can see the context without you re-transcribing it, and its answer isn't added to your history. Any subagent starts without your conversation, so options A, B, and D all require you to paste the trace back in — which is the thing you were trying to avoid.
